content: The Lima Rescue Mission is a city mission located in Lima, Ohio. It was established on November 1, 1906, by Adam Welty. The mission operates entirely on donations and provides essential daily services to homeless and needy individuals in Allen County, Ohio, and its surrounding areas. It is the second-oldest gospel rescue mission in Ohio and the only facility of its kind in west-central Ohio. The mission is affiliated with the Association of Gospel Rescue Missions, which is part of the global city mission movement. On November 1, 1906, Reverend Adam Welty relocated his family from Bluffton, Ohio, to a new residence at 207 East North Street in Lima, Ohio. This large rented house served as both the family’s home and a refuge for transient men in need of food and shelter. Reverend Welty later discovered that their new home was situated in the heart of the city’s “red light district.” Within a few years, the house became insufficient to accommodate the growing number of men seeking assistance. Despite the lack of funds in the mission’s treasury, Reverend Welty determined that a larger building was necessary. Construction began in March 1916, funded in part by $200 that Mrs. Welty had managed to save. However, the construction was temporarily halted during World War I. By June 1920, the mission moved into its spacious new building, which remains in use to this day. In the late 1940s, the Rescue Mission expanded its outreach to include youth ministry through child evangelism classes held in the mission’s chapel. As these classes grew, it became evident that a larger, dedicated space was required. In 1964, a large house, referred to as the Children's Chapel, was purchased to address this need. In 1974, the mission acquired land to establish a new summer day camp, Camp Roberts. This camp, located on 54 acres in Shawnee Township, includes a lodge, a pool, a chapel, and a recreation building.
